title: French protesters clash with police in Paris over living costs and schools
seoTitle: Paris march over living costs and schools

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the high cost of living, rising fuel prices, weak public spending, and poor school conditions.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand higher wages and pensions, lower prices, protection of public services, and better learning conditions.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in Paris and other cities, resulting in at least 166 arrests nationwide.

summary: Demonstrators gathered in Paris and multiple other French cities to protest rising living costs, high fuel prices, and grievances originating from high school student blockades regarding teacher absences and school facilities. The movement drew inspiration from previous social protests, with participants wearing high-visibility vests. In Paris, scuffles erupted near the Place de la République as police deployed tear gas against groups throwing fireworks and other objects. The Interior Ministry reported at least 166 arrests across the country, alongside vandalism and clashes targeting public buildings, media outlets, and police officers in cities including Marseille, Rennes, Toulouse, and Angers. Authorities recorded 140 protests involving tens of thousands of participants outside Paris by midday.
demands: More teachers and decent learning conditions
response: According to the Interior Ministry, police deployed tear gas and large riot forces to disperse crowds, recording at least 166 arrests nationwide. President Emmanuel Macron urged calm, emphasizing the constitutional right to protest alongside the requirement to respect people and property.

arrests.text: at least 166 arrests across the country

updates.text: Police fired tear gas and clashed with protesters in Paris and other French cities during nationwide demonstrations over living costs and school conditions.
